title: From Cantor's Theorem to a Single Point
content: The docstring frames the entry as the uniqueness half the parent left open. Cantor's intersection theorem (the parent's content) guarantees a decreasing sequence of nonempty closed sets in a compact space has nonempty intersection, but says nothing about its size. The Nested Interval Theorem — the form Bolzano and Cantor used to construct ℝ and to prove Bolzano–Weierstrass — adds one hypothesis: if the interval lengths b n − a n → 0, the intersection is a single point. That point is identified concretely as ⨆ₙ a n, the supremum of the left endpoints (equivalently the infimum of the right endpoints). The new mathematical content over the parent is purely the uniqueness, and it is a squeeze: two common points x, y both lie in [a n, b n], so |x − y| ≤ b n − a n → 0.
mathContext: $b_n - a_n \to 0 \Rightarrow \bigcap_n [a_n, b_n] = \{\sup_n a_n\}$ — order-completeness of $\mathbb{R}$ made geometric.

title: Formalizing 'Nested, Shrinking, Complete' as Lean Hypotheses
content: The docstring's prose is turned into exactly four hypotheses: `Monotone a` and `Antitone b` encode 'nested' (each interval contains the next), `∀ n, a n ≤ b n` rules out an interval being empty, and `Tendsto (fun n => b n - a n) atTop (𝓝 0)` encodes 'shrinking'. No compactness or completeness hypothesis is stated explicitly — it is silently supplied by `ℝ` itself, since the proof only ever needs a conditional supremum to exist, which every `BddAbove` set of reals has. The conclusion packages both existence and uniqueness into one equation, `⋂ n, Icc (a n) (b n) = {⨆ n, a n}`, rather than the more common two-step 'is nonempty, and is a singleton'.
mathContext: Hypotheses: $a\nearrow$, $b\searrow$, $a_n\le b_n\ \forall n$, $b_n-a_n\to 0$. Conclusion: $\bigcap_n [a_n,b_n]=\{\sup_n a_n\}$ in one equation.

title: The Cross Bound a m ≤ b n Is the Whole Engine
content: The statement nested_intervals_iInter_singleton takes monotone a, antitone b with a n ≤ b n and lengths → 0. The proof opens by establishing the single cross inequality 'key': a m ≤ b n for ALL m, n regardless of index order, by splitting on m ≤ n vs n ≤ m and threading monotonicity/antitonicity through the diagonal bound a n ≤ b n. This one inequality does double duty for the rest of the proof. Its first consequence: the range of a is bounded above by b 0 (BddAbove (range a)), which is exactly what is needed for the conditional supremum ⨆ₙ a n to exist in ℝ.
mathContext: $\forall m\,n,\ a_m \le b_n$ (split $m\le n$: $a_m\le a_n\le b_n$; $n\le m$: $a_m\le b_m\le b_n$) $\Rightarrow$ range $a$ bounded by $b_0$.

title: Existence: the Supremum Lies in Every Interval
content: The membership half. From the cross bound, le_ciSup gives a n ≤ ⨆ⱼ a j for every n, and ciSup_le gives ⨆ⱼ a j ≤ b n for every n (since every a m ≤ b n). So the supremum sits between a n and b n in every interval, hence belongs to ⋂ₙ [a n, b n]. This is packaged through Set.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem, whose first component is exactly this membership (simp to mem_iInter / mem_Icc). Notably the common point is pinned without ever constructing a limit of a or b — order completeness (ciSup) alone places it.

title: Uniqueness: the Shrinking-Length Squeeze
content: The new content over the parent. Any common point x satisfies a n ≤ x ≤ b n and a n ≤ ⨆ a ≤ b n, so both x and the supremum lie in [a n, b n]; hence |x − ⨆ⱼ a j| ≤ b n − a n for every n (via abs_le, the two bounds discharged by linarith from the interval inequalities). Since b n − a n → 0, ge_of_tendsto' forces |x − ⨆ a| ≤ 0, and abs_nonpos_iff collapses this to x = ⨆ a. This is the squeeze that upgrades 'nonempty' to 'exactly one point'; it is precisely where the shrinking-length hypothesis is used, and the hypothesis is sharp — dropping it (e.g. a ≡ 0, b ≡ 1) leaves the nondegenerate interval [0,1].
mathContext: $|x - \bigsqcup a| \le b_n - a_n \to 0 \Rightarrow |x - \bigsqcup a| \le 0 \Rightarrow x = \bigsqcup a$.

title: Sharpening the Parent's Example to {0}
content: iInter_Icc_zero_one_div_eq_zero specialises the general lemma to give ⋂ₙ [0, 1/(n+1)] = {0} exactly — the parent established only nonemptiness. The instantiation uses constant left endpoint 0 (monotone_const), right endpoint 1/(n+1) shown antitone via one_div_le_one_div_of_le, the nonnegativity a n ≤ b n by positivity, and the shrinking-length hypothesis from tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat. The supremum of the constant-0 left endpoints is 0 by ciSup_const, so the singleton {⨆ a} becomes {0}.
